Why GLP-1 hair falls out
It isn't a vitamin problem. It's a growth-phase problem.

A GLP-1 cuts appetite fast. The body reads that sudden drop in food as a famine, and in a famine it shuts down whatever it doesn't need to stay alive. Hair is 1st in line.

So a huge batch of follicles leaves the growth phase at the same time and goes to rest. Doctors call it telogen effluvium. We call it the Famine Shed.

The hair in the drain today was switched off 2 to 3 months ago.

That delay hides the cause. By the time the clumps show up, nobody connects them to the 1st months of the shot. And because the shot doesn't end like a crash diet does, the famine signal keeps firing. That's why so many women get a 2nd wave.

Step 1
The switch

A huge share of follicles leave the growth phase together and go to rest. Nothing falls yet.

Step 2
The silence

For 2 to 3 months, those hairs sit quietly in the scalp. The hair looks normal. The scale keeps dropping.

Step 3
The shed

The whole batch lets go at once. It peaks around months 4 to 6 and can run 3 to 6 months.

This is now on record
The shot. The shed. The numbers.

In July 2026, the BMJ compared more than 27,000 adults with type 2 diabetes. The GLP-1 group lost hair more often than both groups on other diabetes drugs.

In 1 survey, 20% of GLP-1 users said they had shedding. That's 1 in 5. And nearly 9 in 10 of the people who report it are women.

Most hair advice was never built for this.

The trial
100 adults. 90 days. A placebo group.

Nobody has run a spermidine trial on GLP-1 users yet. Here's what was tested: the exact thing the Famine Shed breaks. Researchers counted how many hairs were still in the active growth phase, then ran it into autumn, the season the body sheds on its own.

Why the usual fixes miss
Every other fix answers the wrong question.
Biotin

Only fixes a biotin shortfall. Most women with this shed have normal labs. The follicles weren't short on supplies. They were switched to rest.

Collagen and protein

Hand the follicle building materials. A follicle switched to rest isn't building anything. Spermidine is the signal to keep building.

DHT blockers

Saw palmetto and pumpkin seed are made for pattern baldness, a hormone problem. The Famine Shed isn't a hormone problem. Spermidine leaves hormones alone.

Minoxidil

A prescription or a greasy scalp, the "dread shed" at the start, and a habit for life. Spermidine is a capsule with no dread shed.

Inside every capsule
1 molecule. 1 job: keep the follicle growing.

Spermidine. 10 mg per serving, sourced from wheat germ. It's a polyamine, not a vitamin. Every cell in the body makes it. Levels fall with age. It shows up in wheat germ, natto, aged cheese, and mushrooms.

{%- if ing_img != blank -%}{%- else -%}Image: the bottle with wheat germ, aged cheese, and mushrooms around it{%- endif -%}
Keeps the hair root dividing

The cells at the base of a growing hair are some of the fastest-dividing cells in the body. They depend on polyamines to keep going. Spermidine keeps them dividing and pushes back the day the follicle quits growing.

Switches on eIF5A

eIF5A is a protein that fast-dividing cells use to keep building. It only turns on with spermidine. No other molecule can do it.

The molecule of lean times

When the body fasts, it raises its own spermidine. Researchers found fasting's cell-cleanup benefit doesn't happen without it.

Works on the measure that matters

In human scalp follicles grown in the lab, spermidine kept more of them in the growth phase. Then the placebo trial confirmed it in people: 52% more growth-phase hairs at 90 days.

What's not inside: no biotin megadose, no saw palmetto, no pumpkin seed, and no hormones. Ingredients: spermidine only. How to take it: 2 capsules a day.

When an untreated shed usually peaks. At 6 months, 0% of the spermidine group had hair come loose on a tug. On placebo: 68%.

Full thickness takes 12 to 18 months, because new hair has to grow out to length. Every month in the growth phase is more length kept.

Questions, answered.
Can [BRAND] be taken with Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, or Zepbound?

[GAP: GLP-1 interaction statement] Spermidine is a polyamine people already eat every day, about 7 to 12 mg from food.

Biotin did nothing. Why would this be different?

Biotin only fixes a biotin shortfall. Most women with this shed have normal labs. Their follicles weren't short on materials. They were switched to rest. Spermidine was tested on exactly that: how many hairs stay in the growth phase.

Won't the hair just grow back on its own?

A lot of it will, eventually. Full thickness takes 12 to 18 months. And as long as the shot keeps appetite low, the famine signal keeps firing. That's why so many women get a 2nd wave. [BRAND] works on keeping follicles growing while the trigger is still there.

Does quitting the shot fix it?

No. Many women quit and keep shedding anyway, because the hairs that fell were switched to rest months earlier. Quitting doesn't flip them back.

Why not minoxidil?

It works for some women. It also means a prescription or a greasy scalp, a "dread shed" at the start, and a habit for life. [BRAND] works on a different lever: it keeps the follicle in the growth phase, with no dread shed.

Isn't this just another vitamin?

No. Spermidine is a polyamine, a molecule every cell makes. It's the only raw material cells can use to switch on eIF5A. No vitamin does that.

Is GLP-1 hair loss permanent?

Most GLP-1 shedding is telogen effluvium, and it's temporary. A smaller group, mostly people with a family history, see pattern hair loss show up. That's a hormone problem, and a different conversation.

How soon does it work?

Hair runs on a 3-month clock. Hairs already at rest on day 1 still fall in the 1st weeks. The trial measured at 90 days and again at 6 months. The fair test is 3 months.

Does it work for men?

Yes. The trial had more men than women. Men on a GLP-1 get the Famine Shed far less often. Loss at the temples or crown is more likely pattern loss.

About the name.

Yes, it was 1st found in semen. That's where the name comes from. Today it comes from wheat germ. It's in every cell in the human body.
